saints.name: Pope St. Silverius
saints.title: Pope and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A pope deposed and exiled for refusing to restore a heretic, who died in banishment for the faith…
biography: Born at Frosinone, the son of Pope Hormisdas before the latter entered the clergy, Silverius was still a subdeacon when the Gothic king Theodahad thrust him into the papal chair; he was consecrated on 8 June 536. His brief pontificate fell amid Justinian's war to wrest Italy from the Goths.

When the general Belisarius entered Rome in December 536, the Empress Theodora demanded that the pope restore Anthimus, the Monophysite patriarch of Constantinople deposed under his predecessor. Silverius refused to reinstate a condemned heretic. Charged then with plotting to surrender the city to the Goths, he was summoned to the Pincian palace in March 537, stripped of the pallium, clothed in a monk's habit, and pronounced deposed.

He was banished first to Patara in Lycia, whose bishop moved Justinian to order his return for a just hearing; but Vigilius, the deacon who had supplanted him by Theodora's favor, shipped him instead to the barren island of Palmarola, where he died of hardship before the close of 537. The Church has honored him from antiquity as a martyr for the faith.
saints.knownFor: Suffering exile rather than betray the faith.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
